## CEO BRIEFING

At 11:42 UTC today, we detected elevated error rates on the Batch API, affecting a subset of customers. The issue was isolated to one of our internal worker fleets. We applied a mitigation at 12:58 by moving all Batch API traffic to a healthy fleet, and error rates have since dropped to near baseline (0.3–0.4% vs. 0.2% baseline). We are currently in a verification window that closes at 14:30 UTC. Root cause is not yet established, but we have two hypotheses under investigation: a change in database connection pool settings in a recent release, and increased load from a large scheduled job. We have not yet tested either. We are monitoring closely and will provide an update after the verification window. For the board call, you can say that we are handling the incident, service is recovering, and we will have more details shortly. Other APIs are unaffected. Affected customers include Contoso, which is a key enterprise account; we are in contact with them.

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

Current status: Incident INC-2026-1109-01 is open, mitigated, verification in progress. All Batch API traffic is on fleet-b; fleet-a is drained and out of rotation. Error rate is 0.3% as of 14:12, baseline 0.2%. Verification window closes at 14:30 UTC.

Open items:
- Root cause not established. Two hypotheses: H1 (connection pool change in r3) and H2 (load from wonka-industries). Neither tested.
- Rollback test for r3 not run.
- Re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete, no failures on re-drive.
- fleet-a not returned to service.

Next steps:
- After verification window closes, we need to test the rollback hypothesis by rolling back r3 on a test fleet or on fleet-a after it's drained, to see if it resolves the issue.
- Investigate the interaction between pool size and load.
- Complete re-drive.
- Once root cause is confirmed, we can plan to return fleet-a to service.

Separate note: Marcus found a security issue (SEC-411) regarding database role over-permission on billing schema. Unrelated to this incident, but needs attention.

We'll keep the engineering team updated.

## CUSTOMER EMAIL

Subject: Update on Batch API incident and your account

Dear Contoso,

We are writing to follow up on your tickets (TKT-8903 and TKT-8907) regarding the elevated error rates on the Batch API earlier today.

We confirm that your account was affected. Between 11:42 and 12:58 UTC, your account made 9,400 Batch API requests, of which 3,410 returned errors (5xx). The first failure occurred at 11:43 and the last at 12:56.

We have applied a mitigation to move all Batch API traffic to a healthy fleet, and error rates have returned to near baseline. We are monitoring the situation and will provide a further update once we have confirmed recovery.

We are also re-driving the failed jobs for affected accounts, and we will ensure that your failed submissions are processed.

Regarding your question about service credits under Schedule B: we will assess monthly availability for the Batch API at the end of the month, as per the contract. If the availability falls below the 99.9% commitment, you will be entitled to a credit as specified in Schedule B. We will provide a detailed report with the availability figure and any applicable credits within 10 business days of month end. You may then submit a claim within 30 days of that publication.

We have noted that your technical contact, Priya Raghunathan, is available. We will coordinate with her if needed.

We apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your patience.

Best regards,
Northstar Support

## STATUS PAGE UPDATE

We are continuing to investigate elevated error rates on the Batch API. We have applied a mitigation to reduce impact, and error rates are returning to normal. We are monitoring the situation closely. Other Northstar APIs are unaffected. We will provide an update by 14:30 UTC.
